text: A colleague says "this variable is 200, so it can't be negative". What is wrong with the sentence, precisely?
choices: The error is that variables hold values rather than patterns, so the premise is backwards.
The variable holds a pattern; 200 is one reading of it, and whether a different reading is negative depends on an agreement the sentence does not state.
Nothing is wrong — 200 is positive under every encoding, so the conclusion holds.
The error is only that 200 might overflow, which would produce a negative value later.
explanation: The pattern 11001000 is 200 unsigned and -56 as a byte. Saying "it is 200" has silently asserted an agreement. This is not pedantry: it is the shape of a real family of bugs, in which a value written under one reading is consumed under another, and nothing in the machine objects because there is nothing there to object.
